name: Deliver a ticket
description: One epic sub-issue from branch to a reviewed PR with green CI: plan → build (TDD) → verify → open PR and CI → independent review ⇄ fix (at most 2 fix rounds). Ends ready for the owner to merge; the owner merges.

inputs.label: Base ref (origin/main, or the parent's origin branch)

inputs.name: stack_line
inputs.label: Stack line for the PR body (empty if not stacked)

states.title: Plan the ticket
states.brief:
You're implementing GitHub issue #{{inputs.issue}} (part of epic #{{inputs.epic}}). This run has its own fresh worktree.

1. Set up the branch: `git fetch origin && git checkout -B {{inputs.branch}} {{inputs.base}}`. The worktree is fresh, so this is safe. Confirm with `git log -1`.
2. Read `gh issue view {{inputs.issue}}` (the approved design and its "Done when" list), `gh issue view {{inputs.epic}}` (background only), `gh issue view 60` (working rules and hotspot files), and `CLAUDE.md`.
3. Use superpowers:writing-plans. Skip brainstorming: the issue is the approved design. Save the plan as `docs/superpowers/plans/<today>-<slug>.md` and commit it. If something is genuinely ambiguous **and** it changes what gets built, set `blocked` to true and explain it in `question`; otherwise make a sensible call and record it in the plan.

House rules (every step):
- Repo `0xvasanth/gespan`. Gespan names only (`src/test/legacyNames.test.ts` must pass). No tool or AI attribution anywhere: no `Co-Authored-By`, no "Generated with".
- Never push to `main`, never push tags, force-push only this run's branch `{{inputs.branch}}` with `--force-with-lease`.
- Stay inside issue #{{inputs.issue}}'s scope; extra work goes under "Follow-ups" in the PR.
- The machine runs many builds in parallel: run long checks one at a time, in the foreground; run `bun install` first if `node_modules` is missing. Known load-flaky tests (the `browser` WebKit video preview, the Windows board "database is locked" test, the diff timing test, `useQuickAttachments` paste, the QuickJS `App.tsx` dead-lock test) must be rerun before you treat them as real failures.
- Quote real result lines for every check; never claim a pass you haven't seen.
- Pilot notes for this ticket: {{inputs.notes?}}

states.title: Build test-first
states.brief:
Implement issue #{{inputs.issue}} on branch `{{inputs.branch}}` by following the plan at `{{states.plan.outputs.plan_path}}`.

Commit as you go. Then use superpowers:requesting-code-review for a fresh self-review, and fix what it finds test-first.

states.title: Open the PR and get CI green
Independent review
states.brief:
You are a reviewer. You didn't write this code: read it fresh, and **don't edit or push the branch**.

Review PR #{{states.open_pr.outputs.pr}} against issue #{{inputs.issue}}.
1. Read #{{inputs.issue}} (scope and "Done when") and the rules in #60.
2. Run the `code-review` skill at high effort on PR {{states.open_pr.outputs.pr}}. Look for correctness bugs, missing or filler tests, scope creep, hotspot edits that aren't small and additive, old product names, attribution, and anything that breaks the other app (Tauri vs Native). Verify each finding against the code before you report it.
3. Check every "Done when" item is covered by a test or a check.
4. If this isn't the first review, also check that each earlier finding was fixed or reasonably declined. The last fix round reported: {{states.fix.outputs.summary?}}
5. Post the findings as **one** comment-only PR review with inline comments (through `gh api`, event `COMMENT`). Never approve or request changes: the owner merges.
Set `verdict` to `pass` (nothing blocking) or `fix`.

House rules (every step):
- Repo `0xvasanth/gespan`. Gespan names only (`src/test/legacyNames.test.ts` must pass). No tool or AI attribution anywhere: no `Co-Authored-By`, no "Generated with".
- Never push to `main`, never push tags, force-push only this run's branch `{{inputs.branch}}` with `--force-with-lease`.
- Stay inside issue #{{inputs.issue}}'s scope; extra work goes under "Follow-ups" in the PR.
- The machine runs many builds in parallel: run long checks one at a time, in the foreground; run `bun install` first if `node_modules` is missing. Known load-flaky tests (the `browser` WebKit video preview, the Windows board "database is locked" test, the diff timing test, `useQuickAttachments` paste, the QuickJS `App.tsx` dead-lock test) must be rerun before you treat them as real failures.
- Quote real result lines for every check; never claim a pass you haven't seen.
- Pilot notes for this ticket: {{inputs.notes?}}

states.title: Fix review findings
states.brief:
Review of PR #{{states.open_pr.outputs.pr}} ({{states.review.outputs.review_url}}) asked for fixes.

Blocking:
{{states.review.outputs.blocking}}

Non-blocking:
{{states.review.outputs.suggestions?}}

Use superpowers:receiving-code-review: check each finding against the code before acting. Fix every blocking finding with a test that fails first. For non-blocking findings, fix the valid, small, in-scope ones; list bigger valid ones under Follow-ups in the PR; decline the ones that don't hold up. Reply to every inline review comment (fixed with commit, deferred, or declined with reasoning). Answer every Cubic comment the same way, but never tag the Cubic bot.

If `{{inputs.base}}` moved, restack onto it. Run {{inputs.checks}} one at a time, push (with `--force-with-lease` only if you rebased), then run `gh pr checks <PR> --watch` until it's green.
